summary: Led a $14M Series A (with Kleiner Perkins) for Mine, a Gen-Z credit-building debit card with an AI 'MoneyGPT' advisor serving ~1M under-30 users.
desc_simple: Mine is a debit card and money app built for young people who want to build a credit score without falling into debt. Unlike a normal credit card it never lets users spend more than they actually have, but it still reports responsible use so they build credit over time. It also includes an AI money coach, 'MoneyGPT', that reviews a user's accounts and gives personalized financial tips.
founders: Carlo Kobe and Scott Smith, Gen-Z college dropouts (originally 'Fizz'), built it via Y Combinator.
financials: $14M Series A (2026); ~1M users (~70% under 30); ~$10M ARR.

summary: Participated in Highlight AI's $40M Series A (led by Khosla) building a shared-intelligence layer across team tools like Slack, Zoom and Linear.
desc_simple: Highlight AI is software that works like a shared memory for a company. It plugs into the everyday tools teams already use — Slack, Figma, Linear and more — and keeps track of what everyone is working on, so both people and their AI assistants can instantly find the context they need instead of constantly asking around. The goal is to make large teams faster and less reliant on hunting for information.
founders: CEO Sergei Sorokin spent ~8 years at Discord as VP of Product, helping grow it from ~5M to 300M monthly users.
financials: $40M Series A (2026).

summary: Joined TwelveLabs' $100M Series B (co-led by NEA and NAVER, with Amazon). TwelveLabs builds AI that semantically searches and indexes video content.
desc_simple: TwelveLabs builds artificial intelligence that can 'watch' and understand video the way a person would. Instead of scrubbing through hours of footage, you type a plain-language question — like 'show me every goal' — and it instantly finds and jumps to those exact moments. It reads the images, actions and sounds in a clip and turns them into something computers can search and organize, which is hugely useful for sports leagues, broadcasters and anyone sitting on massive video libraries.
founders: Jae Lee (co-founder & CEO); founding team of twelve with research backgrounds in language, video and machine learning.
financials: $100M Series B (2026); revenue/valuation not disclosed.

summary: Co-led a $100M Series E for the Premier Lacrosse League (with Joe Tsai); funds media distribution, the Women's Lacrosse League and youth access ahead of LA28.
desc_simple: The Premier Lacrosse League (PLL) is the top professional lacrosse league in North America, where eight touring teams of the world's best players compete in a season carried on ESPN. It makes money from media rights, ticketing, sponsorship and merchandise, and is expanding into women's lacrosse and youth access ahead of the sport's return to the 2028 Olympics.
founders: Brothers Paul Rabil (lacrosse superstar, president) and Mike Rabil (serial entrepreneur, CEO).
financials: $100M Series E (2026) — the largest raise in pro lacrosse history; valuation undisclosed.

summary: TPG (via TPG Sports) agreed to acquire Learfield, the leading college sports commercialization platform serving 1,200+ athletic departments across sponsorship, ticketing and NIL.
desc_simple: Learfield is the company that turns American college sports into a business. For more than 1,200 university athletic departments it sells and manages the advertising, sponsorships, stadium signage and radio/TV broadcast rights — so a school earns money every time its games are watched, attended or sponsored. It's one of the largest and most established players in college sports commercialization.
founders: Founded 1972 by Clyde Lear; today's company formed from the 2018 merger of Learfield and IMG College. CEO Cole Gahagan.
financials: TPG acquiring for ~$2B (2026); annual EBITDA just under $200M; serves 1,200+ athletic departments.

summary: Took a minority stake in Canada's Northern Super League (valued C$85M) — billed as the first PE investment into a pro women's football league.
desc_simple: The Northern Super League is Canada's first professional women's soccer league, with six clubs across the country playing a full season against each other. It was created so Canadian women could play top-flight soccer at home instead of moving abroad, and it earns money from tickets, broadcasts and sponsors — a new, fast-growing property in the rapidly rising women's game.
founders: Diana Matheson, retired Canadian national-team midfielder who scored Canada's bronze-medal goal at the 2012 London Olympics.
financials: APEX investing up to C$30M (~US$21M). Inaugural 2025 season: C$30M+ league revenue, 275,000+ fans across ~80 matches, 16 national partners.

summary: Led a $5M round for ALT Sports Data, a data supplier for alternative/niche sports betting, funding product and international expansion.
desc_simple: ALT Sports Data is the 'official scorekeeper' for smaller, fast-growing sports that the big data companies overlook — think Formula 1, X Games and action sports. It gathers the real-time stats and results for these events and sells that data to betting apps so they can offer wagers, while also running a media platform that helps fans find those bets. Its edge is exclusive data rights to niche sports that competitors don't cover.
founders: Joe Dunnigan (founder).
financials: $5M seed (2025, oversubscribed); exclusive data deals with F1, X Games and 25+ sports properties.

summary: Led a seed round for Cognify Health, an LA medical practice providing virtual youth-athlete concussion consultations within 24 hours.
desc_simple: Cognify Health is a medical practice focused on concussions in young athletes. When a kid takes a hit to the head, families often wait weeks to see a specialist — Cognify instead connects them with a real concussion doctor over video, usually within 24 hours, so injuries are assessed and managed quickly and safely. It pairs telehealth visits with clear return-to-play guidance for parents, coaches and schools.
founders: Christian Juzang, a Harvard graduate with venture experience, started it after his sister's volleyball head injury exposed slow concussion care.
financials: 'Multi-million' seed round; amount undisclosed.

summary: Acquired a 49% stake in Sweden's FC Rosengård to become the club's largest outside shareholder — its second women's-club investment.
desc_simple: FC Rosengård is Sweden's most successful women's soccer club, based in Malmö, with a long history of league titles and world-class players. It operates as a professional women's football business focused on match-day, competition and commercial growth, and is now bringing in professional management to raise its game on and off the pitch.
founders: Member-run association retains majority; Crux Football (founded by Rebecca Smith) is largest outside shareholder; ex-Sweden captain Caroline Seger is Head of Football.
financials: Crux acquired 49% (Jan 2026); terms undisclosed.

summary: Invested in Pickleball One, a company operating a comprehensive pickleball business.
desc_simple: Pickleball One is a Japanese company built entirely around pickleball, one of the world's fastest-growing racket sports. It runs a popular news and information website, sells paddles and gear through an online store, and organizes lessons, events and community activities to grow the sport in Japan. It's an early but revenue-generating business aiming to become the hub for pickleball in its market.
financials: Seed round April 2026 (undisclosed); revenue-generating; Tokyo-based.

summary: Made its first WNBA investment, joining new investors in Cleveland's 2028 expansion franchise.
desc_simple: Cleveland's new professional women's basketball team, set to start playing in the WNBA in 2028 at the Cavaliers' downtown arena. It brings top-level women's basketball back to Cleveland for the first time in about 25 years, and fans can already put down deposits to reserve season tickets.
founders: Majority owner Dan Gilbert (founder of Rock Entertainment Group, owner of the Cleveland Cavaliers); Monarch Collective, a women's-sports investment firm, made its first WNBA investment here.
financials: 16th WNBA franchise; $250M expansion fee, ~$290M post-money valuation; debuts 2028; Gilbert group ~54.6%, Monarch ~16.3%; 8,000+ season-ticket deposits.

summary: Co-led (with Neo) Liquid's $18M Series A — a 24/7 leveraged-trading platform spanning stocks, crypto, commodities and prediction markets.
desc_simple: Liquid is a single app where people can trade many different things around the clock. Users can buy and sell stocks, crypto, currencies, commodities, prediction-market bets and even shares of companies before they go public, and can use borrowed money (leverage) to make bigger bets. The goal is to put many markets in one place so traders don't need lots of separate apps.
founders: Franklyn Wang (CEO), a 25-year-old Harvard graduate who was a quantitative researcher at hedge fund Two Sigma before founding Liquid.
financials: $18M Series A (Apr 2026), co-led by Neo and Left Lane; prior $7.6M seed (2025) led by Paradigm; leverage up to 200x in some markets.

summary: Led a $50M Series B in Italian legal-tech Lexroom, building a legal AI engine for civil-law Europe.
desc_simple: Lexroom builds an AI assistant for lawyers in 'civil law' countries across continental Europe. Instead of guessing like a normal chatbot, it searches a verified library of 6M+ real laws, court rulings and regulations, so its answers cite genuine sources. Law firms and company legal teams use it to do legal research faster and more reliably.
founders: Paolo Fois (CEO & co-founder); Milan-based.
financials: $50M Series B (May 2026) led by Left Lane; ~€16.2M Series A ~8 months earlier; ~$73M total raised; 8,000+ law firms and legal teams as customers.

summary: Backed BetHog's ~$10M Series A, funding a crypto casino's AI-powered live-dealer studio platform.
desc_simple: BetHog is an online casino and sportsbook where people bet using cryptocurrency instead of regular money. Its standout feature is AI-powered live-dealer games, where a computer-generated dealer runs games like blackjack in many languages instead of a real person on camera. It works in 14 languages, accepts 10 cryptocurrencies, and has spun out an arm that sells its AI-dealer tech to other casinos.
founders: Nigel Eccles (CEO & co-founder), who previously co-founded and led fantasy-sports and betting giant FanDuel.
financials: $10M Series A (Apr 2026), co-led by Will Ventures and RockawayX; ~$16M total funding.

summary: Invested in PlayerData, a Scottish athlete-tracking company (GPS wearables, smart balls, video analysis) — its fifth portfolio company.
desc_simple: PlayerData is a Scottish company that makes technology to track and improve athlete performance. It sells small GPS wearable trackers, 'smart' balls with GPS chips inside (built with Puma and Mitre), and a portable 8K AI camera that analyzes game video. Coaches use it to boost performance and cut injury risk, at a price cheaper than elite pro systems.
founders: Roy Hotrabhvanon (CEO) and Hayden Ball, University of Edinburgh computer-science grads (founded 2017); Hotrabhvanon is a former international archer.
financials: $12M Series A (~Jun 2026); AO Ventures invested Jul 2026 (undisclosed); ~40% growth over 18 months; FIFA Preferred Provider, trackers worn by officials at World Cup matches.

summary: Exercised an option to invest in ScorePlay, an AI media/asset-management platform used by 300+ organizations and deployed at the Australian Open 2026.
desc_simple: ScorePlay is software that helps sports teams, leagues and brands manage all their photos, videos and live footage in one place. Its AI automatically tags and organizes the content so staff can instantly find, share and post the right clips, even translated into different languages — saving media teams huge time during games and events.
founders: Victorien Tixier (CEO) and Xavier Green co-founded ScorePlay in 2021; the pair previously built and exited a sports-tech startup and were named to Forbes 30 Under 30.
financials: $13M Series A (Feb 2025), ~$20M total; used by 300+ sports organizations; ~3x YoY growth and profitable; AO Ventures invested Jul 2026.

summary: Completed a transaction to become majority shareholder of Atlético de Madrid, with up to €100M of additional equity approved for teams and infrastructure.
desc_simple: Atlético de Madrid is a professional football club in Madrid, Spain, that plays in La Liga, the country's top league. Founded in 1903, it's one of Spain's biggest and most successful clubs, with a large global fanbase and men's, women's and youth teams.
founders: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín remains CEO and Enrique Cerezo Chairman after Apollo took majority control; club founded 1903.
financials: Apollo Sports Capital became majority shareholder (Mar 2026); board approved up to €100M additional equity; valuation undisclosed.

summary: Participated in Splose's $46M Series A (led by Spectrum Equity); Splose is allied-health practice-management software used by 20,000+ practitioners.
desc_simple: Splose is software that helps allied-health practices — physiotherapists, psychologists, speech therapists — run their day-to-day business. Its AI handles booking appointments, patient records, invoices, payments and reports, so practitioners spend less time on paperwork and more time with patients.
founders: Nicholas Sanderson (founder & CEO); based in Adelaide, Australia.
financials: A$46M Series A led by Spectrum Equity (Feb 2026); 20,000+ practitioners across Australia, UK and NZ; 100%+ YoY growth.

fund_name: Blue Owl Capital - Dyal HomeCourt Partners
summary: Acquired a minority stake in the Cleveland Cavaliers (Gilbert retains majority) — the fund's sixth NBA franchise investment.
desc_simple: The Cleveland Cavaliers are a professional basketball team in the NBA, based in Cleveland, Ohio. They compete against other franchises across the US and Canada and play home games at a downtown Cleveland arena — one of the league's 30 clubs.
founders: Dan Gilbert remains majority owner through his ROCK Family of Companies; Blue Owl's HomeCourt fund holds a minority stake.
financials: Blue Owl's HomeCourt fund took a minority stake (Jul 2026); size/valuation undisclosed; sixth NBA team in the fund's portfolio.

summary: Made a $30M strategic investment in Selkirk Sport, a leading pickleball equipment and apparel brand — its ninth portfolio deal.
desc_simple: Selkirk Sport designs and makes pickleball gear — paddles, balls, nets, shoes and clothing. It runs its own manufacturing and sells online and through major retailers like Target, Costco and Amazon, making it one of the leading equipment brands in the fast-growing sport of pickleball.
founders: Founded 2014 by Idaho's Barnes family — brothers Mike and Rob Barnes (Co-CEOs) and Tom Barnes (R&D), with father Jim as President — starting from a passion for pickleball.
financials: $30M growth investment from Bluestone (Jan 2026) at ~$200M valuation; revenue up ~1,900% since 2019; projected 2026 revenue $100M+; first outside capital.

summary: Acquired ~15% of UK promoter Matchroom (boxing, PDC darts, World Snooker) at a £1bn+ valuation to fuel US expansion.
desc_simple: Matchroom is a British company that stages live sports events and makes TV shows about them. It organises professional boxing, PDC darts and World Snooker competitions — hundreds of events a year — and sells the broadcasts worldwide. It also manages and promotes stars like boxers Anthony Joshua and Katie Taylor and darts champion Luke Littler.
founders: Barry Hearn founded Matchroom in 1982; son Eddie Hearn (chairman) built the boxing business. The Hearn family keeps majority control.
financials: Bruin took a ~15% minority stake (May 2026) at a £1bn+ valuation; produces 600+ events and 2,400+ hours of programming a year.

summary: CVC's Global Sport Group agreed to acquire a controlling stake in Equine Network, the largest US for-profit equestrian league — GSG's eighth league.
desc_simple: Equine Network runs the largest for-profit collection of horse-riding sports competitions in the US. It owns and operates roughly 40 of its own contests and sanctions 800+ others across Western and English riding, and provides media, membership and other services — essentially a sports-league business built around competitive horseback riding.
founders: Founder and CEO Tom Winsor built and still leads the company; ex-WWE presidents Michelle Wilson and George Barrios expected to become Co-Chairs.
financials: CVC's Global Sport Group agreed to acquire a controlling stake (Jan 2026, ~US$300M), expected to close Q2 2026; ~40 owned + 800+ sanctioned events.

summary: Participated in PvX Partners' $10.5M Series A; PvX provides cohort financing and market intelligence for consumer apps.
desc_simple: PvX Partners provides money and data insights to companies that make mobile games and consumer apps. When a developer needs cash to run ads and attract users, PvX funds that spending and gets paid back from the revenue those users generate, using machine-learning tools to predict which campaigns will pay off — so app makers grow faster without giving away ownership.
founders: Co-founded 2024 by CEO Joe Wadakethalakal (ex-JP Morgan, ZM Capital, president at mobile-gaming firm MPL) with Ridzki Syahputera and Zhen Jie Sim; Singapore-based.
financials: $10.5M Series A (Apr 2026); $250M+ committed user-acquisition financing by Oct 2025, plus $500M more committed; previously raised $3.8M.

summary: Joined SportIQ's $6.2M Series A (with KB Partners); SportIQ makes connected basketballs with a valve-mounted shot-tracking sensor.
desc_simple: SportIQ makes a real basketball with a tiny sensor hidden inside the ball's valve, so it looks and plays like a normal ball. The sensor tracks how you shoot — position, power and angle of each shot — and sends it to a phone app that gives feedback and tips. It's designed for basketball players of all levels who want to practise smarter.
founders: Harri Hohteri (founder & Chief Product Officer); Helsinki, Finland-based.
financials: $6.2M Series A (Feb 2026, across two closings); sensor built into the Spalding TF DNA basketball; protected by multiple patents.

summary: Participated in Tokaido Health's $25M Series A (led by Norwest); an AI medication-navigation platform.
desc_simple: Tokaido Health uses AI to help people find cheaper medicines that work just as well as the ones they take. It looks at a person's medical situation, insurance drug list and location to suggest lower-cost options, adds rewards to encourage switching, and plugs into the systems health plans and pharmacy managers already use.
founders: Ben Ryugo (founder & CEO), previously at care-navigation company Included Health; co-founders include Jacob Crothers, Andrew Ashinohara and Samir Koppolu.
financials: $25M Series A led by Norwest (May 2026); emerged from stealth with the raise.

summary: Otro-owned FlexWork Sports acquired youth camp operator ProCamps (175+ events/yr) and its G3 Marketing arm.
desc_simple: ProCamps runs sports camps and events where kids and fans train with and meet professional and college athletes. Each event has hands-on instruction plus Q&As, photos and casual time with the athletes, so participants leave with real memories. It puts on 175+ events a year, and its G3 Marketing arm builds branded fan experiences.
founders: Co-founder Gregg Darbyshire (now FlexWork Chief Growth Officer), with a long history hosting fantasy-sports events featuring top college coaches.
financials: Acquired by Otro-owned FlexWork Sports in an 8-figure deal (Jun 2026); 175+ events/year.

summary: Participated in Israeli web-security startup Huskeys' $8M seed (with 10D, SV Angel and athlete investors).
desc_simple: Huskeys makes software that protects websites from hackers. Instead of replacing the security systems companies already use, it adds an AI layer on top that studies web traffic to tell real customers apart from attackers — so fewer real users get wrongly blocked while genuine threats are stopped. It's built for large companies running big websites.
founders: Itai Gafni (CEO) and Roy Weisfeld (CTO), both alumni of Israel's elite Unit 8200, specializing in AI and web security.
financials: $8M seed (Mar 2026); customers include TikTok, Merlin Entertainments and Hugging Face; processes 1T+ traffic requests across tens of thousands of domains.

summary: PLUS athlete members (Klay Thompson, Marcus Smart, DK Metcalf) joined Bathhouse's $35M round (led by Imaginary Ventures).
desc_simple: Bathhouse is a chain of social spa venues built around heat and cold. Visitors move between saunas, steam rooms, warm pools and cold plunges, and can join group ceremonies that mix heat, essential oils and music. It also offers massages, scrubs and a healthy-food restaurant — a place to relax, socialize and recover, alone or with friends.
founders: Travis Talmadge (co-founder).
financials: $35M round led by Imaginary Ventures (28 investors), May 2026; three NYC locations, expanding toward ~10 nationwide (LA, Chicago, Nashville).

summary: Founding investor in the Upshot League, a new women's developmental basketball circuit that raised $40M from 90+ backers.
desc_simple: The UpShot League is a new professional women's basketball league in the southeastern US. It gives college graduates and other players a place to keep competing when there aren't enough WNBA roster spots, acting as a developmental step toward the top league. Its first season starts May 2026 with four teams playing a 40-game schedule, streamed live on YouTube.
founders: Founded by Andy Kaufmann (CEO of Zawyer Sports & Entertainment) with co-founder and commissioner Donna Orender, a former WNBA president.
financials: ~$40M raised from 90+ backers (May 2026); 4 inaugural teams; 40-game season debuting May 15, 2026.

summary: Led by ex-NFL players Terrence Murphy and Reggie Bush, acquired operating rights to LOVB Salt Lake via a $150M target fund.
desc_simple: LOVB Salt Lake is the Salt Lake City team in League One Volleyball (LOVB), a top US professional women's volleyball league. Its roster features Olympians and stars from 20+ countries competing against other pro teams. LOVB links youth clubs, college recruiting and this pro league in one system, giving young players a path to the professional level.
founders: Led by Synergy Sports Capital's Terrence C. Murphy Sr. (former NFL wide receiver and real-estate entrepreneur) and Reggie Bush (former NFL running back and Heisman winner).
financials: Synergy Sports Capital (a $150M PE fund) acquired operating rights (Mar 2026); deal value undisclosed.

summary: 35V partnered with TPA Group to acquire the 515-acre former Six Flags America site in Maryland for mixed-use redevelopment.
desc_simple: This is a project to rebuild a 515-acre piece of land in Prince George's County, Maryland, that was the Six Flags America amusement park before it closed in 2025. Instead of rides, the plan is a large 'mixed-use' community that could combine homes, offices, shops and other facilities in one area, aiming to bring new jobs and activity to the neighborhoods.
founders: Led by Kevin Durant's Thirty Five Ventures (co-founded 2016 with Rich Kleiman; Durant grew up nearby in Seat Pleasant, MD); development partner TPA Group is an Atlanta real-estate developer.
financials: 515-acre site; redevelopment announced 2026 (park closed Nov 2025); purchase price undisclosed.

summary: With Bolt Ventures and Main Street Advisors (led by Guenther Steiner), completed the acquisition of the Tech3 MotoGP team.
desc_simple: Tech3 is a French motorcycle racing team, started in 1989, that competes in MotoGP and Moto3 — the top championships of Grand Prix motorcycle racing. The team enters riders and specially built racing motorcycles in races worldwide and is known for developing talent, racing as Red Bull KTM Tech3.
founders: Founded 1989 by Hervé Poncharal (with Guy Coulon), who ran it for 36 years; new CEO is Guenther Steiner, a former Formula 1 team principal.
financials: Acquisition completed Jan 2026 (~€20M reported); price not officially disclosed.

summary: InStudio's $50M sports fund is anchored by small minority stakes in the Buffalo Bills and LA Chargers plus a stake in the Aston Martin F1 team.
desc_simple: This is a sports investment fund that does two things at once. It owns tiny slices of famous pro teams — the Buffalo Bills and LA Chargers in the NFL and the Aston Martin Formula 1 team — which brings credibility and connections. And, where it expects most of its returns, it invests in young technology companies that build tools for sports, like AI that analyzes athlete health and performance.
founders: Founder and managing partner Danny Cortenraede, an LA-based investor with a Harvard executive MBA.
financials: $50M fund launched Apr 2026; targets ~$3M per company in Series A+ startups with $1M+ ARR; ~65% of investors are pro athletes.

summary: Participated in Rematch's $3.5M round building global media infrastructure for grassroots sports highlights; first invested May 2024.
desc_simple: Rematch is a media platform that captures and shares highlight videos from amateur and youth sports games that normally never get filmed. Parents, fans and volunteers record local games on their phones, and Rematch's AI tools edit the footage into shareable highlight clips — built for grassroots sports communities (soccer, flag football, volleyball) and their families.
founders: Co-founded 2017 in Bordeaux, France by CEO Pierre Husson; US operations (Fort Worth, TX) led by US CEO Hanna Howard.
financials: $3.5M round (Jun 2026); 1B+ organic views globally; $1.2M+ annual revenue; millions of user-created videos.

summary: Invested in Athletes.org, a players'-association platform for college athletes.
desc_simple: Athletes.org (AO) is a players' association for US college athletes — a group that helps them organize, learn their rights and speak with one collective voice. It educates and represents members, pushes for collective bargaining, and gives athletes free resources plus tools like a system to rate their schools, since college athletes generate huge revenue but historically had no organized body.
founders: Founded 2023 by Jim Cavale (chairman; previously founded athlete-marketing company INFLCR) with former NFL player Brandon Copeland.
financials: One growth financing round (2026, JDS Sports); amount undisclosed.

desc_simple: Poolhouse builds high-tech pool and billiards venues where people play cue sports as a fun night out. A camera-and-software system called BillyQ watches the table and adds digital effects on top of it, so scoring happens automatically and players of different skill levels can compete fairly — turning an ordinary pool table into an interactive game you play with real balls and cues.
founders: Steve & Dave Jolliffe (co-creators of Topgolf and Puttshack) and Paul Hawkins (founder of Hawk-Eye ball-tracking); CEO Andrew O'Brien.
financials: $55M growth round (Jul 2026).
summary: Poolhouse builds high-tech pool and billiards venues where people play cue sports as a fun night out. A camera-and-software system called BillyQ watches the table and adds digital effects on top of it, so scoring happens automatically and players of different skill levels can compete fairly — turning an ordinary pool table into an interactive game you play with real balls and cues.

desc_simple: Full Swing makes golf simulators and launch monitors — machines that let people play golf indoors. Players hit a real ball into a screen while sensors measure the shot and show it playing out on a virtual version of famous courses. It is the official licensed simulator of the PGA Tour, and its tech can also simulate sports like baseball and soccer.
founders: Founded 2015 by George Pyne, a sports-business executive who later founded Bruin Capital (the prior owner).
financials: Acquired by Versant for ~$530M (Jul 2026); Bruin bought a controlling stake in 2019 for ~$160M.
summary: Full Swing makes golf simulators and launch monitors — machines that let people play golf indoors. Players hit a real ball into a screen while sensors measure the shot and show it playing out on a virtual version of famous courses. It is the official licensed simulator of the PGA Tour, and its tech can also simulate sports like baseball and soccer.

desc_simple: The Seattle Seahawks are a professional American football team in the NFL. They represent the city of Seattle and compete each season against other NFL teams, aiming to win the Super Bowl.
financials: ~$9.6B sale (Jul 2026) — a record for a US sports team; valued ~$6.59B a year earlier.
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are a professional American football team in the NFL. They represent the city of Seattle and compete each season against other NFL teams, aiming to win the Super Bowl.

desc_simple: Cosm builds giant dome-shaped venues with huge curved LED screens that wrap around the audience. Inside, people watch live sports, concerts and movies in a way that feels like being inside the action — what the company calls 'shared reality' — with venues in cities like Los Angeles and Dallas.
founders: Stephen Winn built Cosm into its current immersive shared-reality form from 2020.
financials: ~$100M investment from Sony Pictures (Jun 2026).
summary: Cosm builds giant dome-shaped venues with huge curved LED screens that wrap around the audience. Inside, people watch live sports, concerts and movies in a way that feels like being inside the action — what the company calls 'shared reality' — with venues in cities like Los Angeles and Dallas.

desc_simple: Detroit City FC is a professional soccer club in the USL Championship, known for its passionate fans and community roots. It started as a small grassroots team in 2012 and has grown into a pro organization, and is building AlumniFi Field, a new 15,000-seat stadium.
founders: Co-founder and CEO Sean Mann helped launch the club in 2012 as a community-focused grassroots team.
financials: Largest single investment in club history (amount undisclosed); anchoring a $150M stadium within a ~$200M mixed-use development.
summary: Detroit City FC is a professional soccer club in the USL Championship, known for its passionate fans and community roots. It started as a small grassroots team in 2012 and has grown into a pro organization, and is building AlumniFi Field, a new 15,000-seat stadium.

desc_simple: Kalshi is a US-regulated exchange where people buy and sell simple 'yes or no' contracts on whether real-world events will happen — like which team wins a game. If your prediction is right, the contract pays out, working a bit like a stock market for future events.
founders: Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, MIT graduates who worked in finance before starting the company.
financials: $1B round (May 2026) at a ~$22B valuation.
summary: Kalshi is a US-regulated exchange where people buy and sell simple 'yes or no' contracts on whether real-world events will happen — like which team wins a game. If your prediction is right, the contract pays out, working a bit like a stock market for future events.

desc_simple: EDGE Markets builds the money 'plumbing' behind sports-betting and prediction-market apps — banking and payment systems that move customer deposits and payouts quickly and cheaply, plus a debit-card program built for bettors.
founders: Seni Thomas (founder and CEO).
financials: $29.2M Series A (Jun 2026); its EDGE Boost card has processed $2B+.
summary: EDGE Markets builds the money 'plumbing' behind sports-betting and prediction-market apps — banking and payment systems that move customer deposits and payouts quickly and cheaply, plus a debit-card program built for bettors.

desc_simple: Venezia FC is a professional Italian soccer club based in the canal city of Venice, known for its stylish kits and passionate local fans. It competes in the Italian league system and is working on plans for a new stadium.
financials: Strategic minority investment within a €100M (~$118M) fundraise.
summary: Venezia FC is a professional Italian soccer club based in the canal city of Venice, known for its stylish kits and passionate local fans. It competes in the Italian league system and is working on plans for a new stadium.

desc_simple: The X Games League is a new professional action-sports league where teams of skateboarders, snowboarders, skiers and BMX riders compete, each roster split evenly between men and women, with every city fielding a summer and a winter team. UNA Sports Group bought its New York franchises.
financials: Eight-figure acquisition (May 2026); league owned by MSP Sports Capital.
summary: The X Games League is a new professional action-sports league where teams of skateboarders, snowboarders, skiers and BMX riders compete, each roster split evenly between men and women, with every city fielding a summer and a winter team. UNA Sports Group bought its New York franchises.

desc_simple: The Las Vegas Raiders are a professional American football team in the NFL, playing at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. They compete each season against other NFL teams aiming to reach the Super Bowl.
financials: A Silver Lake-led group acquired ~25% at an ~$11B valuation; Mark Davis retains control.
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are a professional American football team in the NFL, playing at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. They compete each season against other NFL teams aiming to reach the Super Bowl.

desc_simple: The Rajasthan Royals are a professional cricket team in the Indian Premier League, India's biggest and richest cricket competition. Based in Jaipur, they play fast-paced Twenty20 matches against other city teams before huge crowds and TV audiences.
financials: Valued ~$1.65B (May 2026).
summary: The Rajasthan Royals are a professional cricket team in the Indian Premier League, India's biggest and richest cricket competition. Based in Jaipur, they play fast-paced Twenty20 matches against other city teams before huge crowds and TV audiences.

desc_simple: Royal Challengers Bengaluru is one of the most popular teams in the Indian Premier League and also fields a Women's Premier League side. Based in Bengaluru, it plays Twenty20 cricket with a massive, devoted fan following.
financials: Blackstone-led group acquired it for ~$1.78B from Diageo's United Spirits (Mar 2026).
summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru is one of the most popular teams in the Indian Premier League and also fields a Women's Premier League side. Based in Bengaluru, it plays Twenty20 cricket with a massive, devoted fan following.

desc_simple: LiveMode is an international sports streaming service connected to Brazil's popular CazéTV. It shows live sports for free through YouTube and social media, so fans worldwide can watch games on phones and computers without a traditional TV subscription.
financials: Cristiano Ronaldo took a significant stake (May 2026); amount undisclosed.
summary: LiveMode is an international sports streaming service connected to Brazil's popular CazéTV. It shows live sports for free through YouTube and social media, so fans worldwide can watch games on phones and computers without a traditional TV subscription.

desc_simple: Olympique Lyonnais ('Lyon') is a major French soccer club with famous men's and women's teams; its women's side is one of the most successful in the world. The club plays in France's top divisions and competes in Europe.
financials: Michele Kang (owner of the Washington Spirit and other women's clubs) agreed to buy Lyon (Jun 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: Olympique Lyonnais ('Lyon') is a major French soccer club with famous men's and women's teams; its women's side is one of the most successful in the world. The club plays in France's top divisions and competes in Europe.

desc_simple: Working Capital Partners runs a financing platform that gives pro athletes cash advances against their future contract earnings, so an athlete can get money upfront and repay it from their salary instead of waiting years.
financials: Series A led by WTSL, a Silver Lake-backed firm (Mar 2026); amount undisclosed.
summary: Working Capital Partners runs a financing platform that gives pro athletes cash advances against their future contract earnings, so an athlete can get money upfront and repay it from their salary instead of waiting years.

desc_simple: Inner Circle Sports is a boutique investment bank that advises on buying and selling sports teams and sports businesses, helping arrange deals and the finances behind them.
financials: Acquired by investment bank William Blair (May 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: Inner Circle Sports is a boutique investment bank that advises on buying and selling sports teams and sports businesses, helping arrange deals and the finances behind them.

desc_simple: ViewLift builds the technology behind sports and entertainment streaming apps, giving teams, leagues and media companies the tools to stream their games directly to fans and handle subscriptions and advertising.
financials: Acquired by DAZN for ~$100M (May 2026).
summary: ViewLift builds the technology behind sports and entertainment streaming apps, giving teams, leagues and media companies the tools to stream their games directly to fans and handle subscriptions and advertising.

desc_simple: The Pittsburgh Penguins are a professional ice hockey team in the NHL, playing at PPG Paints Arena and competing each season for the Stanley Cup.
financials: Sold by Fenway Sports Group to the Hoffmann family for ~$1.7B (2026).
summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins are a professional ice hockey team in the NHL, playing at PPG Paints Arena and competing each season for the Stanley Cup.

desc_simple: MLSE is a Canadian company that owns Toronto's biggest sports teams — the Raptors (NBA), Maple Leafs (NHL) and Toronto FC — and runs the arenas, broadcasts and events around them.
financials: Rogers acquired the remaining ~25% for ~$3.06B to take full ownership (Jul 2026).
summary: MLSE is a Canadian company that owns Toronto's biggest sports teams — the Raptors (NBA), Maple Leafs (NHL) and Toronto FC — and runs the arenas, broadcasts and events around them.

desc_simple: Teamworks makes software and AI tools that sports teams and athletic departments use to run day-to-day operations — scheduling practices, messaging players, tracking training and organizing the many tasks of managing a team, across pro and college sports.
founders: Zach Maurides, founder and CEO who started it as a Duke football player to help teams manage scheduling and communication.
financials: $200M round (May 2026) at a $1.5B+ valuation.
summary: Teamworks makes software and AI tools that sports teams and athletic departments use to run day-to-day operations — scheduling practices, messaging players, tracking training and organizing the many tasks of managing a team, across pro and college sports.

desc_simple: Swsh collects the photos and videos fans take at concerts, games and live events, then uses AI to sort them into searchable albums and spot things like logos and merchandise — so brands and teams can see what really happened at their events.
founders: Alexandra Debow, a Thiel Fellow who first built Swsh as a college photo-sharing app before pivoting to live events.
financials: $4M seed (Jun 2026).
summary: Swsh collects the photos and videos fans take at concerts, games and live events, then uses AI to sort them into searchable albums and spot things like logos and merchandise — so brands and teams can see what really happened at their events.

desc_simple: The New Zealand SailGP team, the Black Foils, competes in SailGP — a global league where high-speed foiling sailboats race around the world. The team represents New Zealand and includes some of sailing's top Olympic champions.
financials: MSP Sports Capital acquired a majority stake (Jun 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: The New Zealand SailGP team, the Black Foils, competes in SailGP — a global league where high-speed foiling sailboats race around the world. The team represents New Zealand and includes some of sailing's top Olympic champions.

desc_simple: X Games Club São Paulo is a team in the X Games League, a competition built around action sports like skateboarding and BMX. Based in São Paulo, it brings the X Games brand to fans in Brazil.
financials: Acquired by Summit Ventures (Jun 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: X Games Club São Paulo is a team in the X Games League, a competition built around action sports like skateboarding and BMX. Based in São Paulo, it brings the X Games brand to fans in Brazil.

desc_simple: Swansea City is a professional soccer club based in Swansea, Wales, that plays in England's competitive league system, with a long history and a loyal local fan base.
financials: Shamrock Capital took a minority stake (Jul 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: Swansea City is a professional soccer club based in Swansea, Wales, that plays in England's competitive league system, with a long history and a loyal local fan base.

desc_simple: The Texas Junior Golf Tour is a golf circuit for young players in Texas, organizing tournaments where junior golfers compete and develop — one of the top regional youth golf tours in the state.
financials: Acquired by Bolt Ventures (Jun 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: The Texas Junior Golf Tour is a golf circuit for young players in Texas, organizing tournaments where junior golfers compete and develop — one of the top regional youth golf tours in the state.

desc_simple: Tapin2 makes self-service ordering technology for stadiums and venues, so fans can order food and drinks from their phones or kiosks instead of waiting in long lines.
financials: Majority buyout by Greater Sum Ventures (May 2026).
summary: Tapin2 makes self-service ordering technology for stadiums and venues, so fans can order food and drinks from their phones or kiosks instead of waiting in long lines.

desc_simple: Nextiles builds tiny sensors directly into fabric to make smart, wearable sports gear that measures how an athlete moves and performs, helping track performance and prevent injuries.
founders: George Sun, founder and CEO with a background in materials science and wearable technology.
financials: Acquired by Betterguards (May 2026).
summary: Nextiles builds tiny sensors directly into fabric to make smart, wearable sports gear that measures how an athlete moves and performs, helping track performance and prevent injuries.

desc_simple: ONIT makes officially-licensed trading cards for college athletes across hundreds of university teams, photographing and producing cards of individual student-athletes for fans and collectors — and is known for making more women's-sports cards than its competitors.
financials: Works with 8,000+ athletes across 212 teams.
summary: ONIT makes officially-licensed trading cards for college athletes across hundreds of university teams, photographing and producing cards of individual student-athletes for fans and collectors — and is known for making more women's-sports cards than its competitors.

desc_simple: This is the New York team in a new professional women's golf league where top female golfers compete in a fast-paced, team-based, prime-time format created to give women's golf a modern, team-based competition.
financials: Team valuations reported ~$20M each; terms undisclosed.
summary: This is the New York team in a new professional women's golf league where top female golfers compete in a fast-paced, team-based, prime-time format created to give women's golf a modern, team-based competition.

desc_simple: RCX Sports runs official youth sports programs on behalf of major pro leagues — NFL Flag, MLS GO, Jr. NBA and Jr. WNBA, MLB Pitch Hit & Run and NHL Street — giving large numbers of kids a way to play organized versions of the sports they love.
financials: Operates within a ~$70B youth sports market; previously owned by The Raine Group.
summary: RCX Sports runs official youth sports programs on behalf of major pro leagues — NFL Flag, MLS GO, Jr. NBA and Jr. WNBA, MLB Pitch Hit & Run and NHL Street — giving large numbers of kids a way to play organized versions of the sports they love.

desc_simple: A new mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion that stages professional cage-fighting events and builds them into a global TV and streaming product. Launching in early 2027, it aims to compete with leagues like the UFC by signing fighters and distributing events worldwide.
founders: Scott Coker, a veteran MMA promoter who previously founded Strikeforce and led Bellator MMA.
financials: $60M raise (May 2026); launch targeted for early 2027.
summary: A new mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion that stages professional cage-fighting events and builds them into a global TV and streaming product. Launching in early 2027, it aims to compete with leagues like the UFC by signing fighters and distributing events worldwide.

desc_simple: The Brampton Honey Badgers are a professional basketball team in the Canadian Elite Basketball League, based in Brampton, Ontario, competing against other Canadian pro teams (2022 league champions).
financials: Mark Cuban took a minority stake (May 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: The Brampton Honey Badgers are a professional basketball team in the Canadian Elite Basketball League, based in Brampton, Ontario, competing against other Canadian pro teams (2022 league champions).

desc_simple: Pickleball Inc. is the parent company behind much of professional pickleball — it owns Major League Pickleball and the PPA Tour, plus businesses that sell equipment, provide tournament software and build courts, making it a one-stop operator across the pro pickleball world.
founders: Samin Odhwani is MLP commissioner; Tom Dundon (Dundon Capital) is a lead backer and owner of the NHL's Carolina Hurricanes.
financials: $225M growth round at a ~$750M valuation (May 2026); ~$140M 2025 ecosystem revenue.
summary: Pickleball Inc. is the parent company behind much of professional pickleball — it owns Major League Pickleball and the PPA Tour, plus businesses that sell equipment, provide tournament software and build courts, making it a one-stop operator across the pro pickleball world.

desc_simple: The San Francisco Giants are a Major League Baseball team based in San Francisco, competing in the National League West and playing at their downtown ballpark.
financials: Thrive Capital took a minority stake; team valued ~$4B; terms undisclosed.
summary: The San Francisco Giants are a Major League Baseball team based in San Francisco, competing in the National League West and playing at their downtown ballpark.

desc_simple: The San Diego Padres are a Major League Baseball team based in San Diego, competing in the National League West and earning through tickets, media rights and sponsorships.
founders: New lead buyer José E. Feliciano co-founded PE firm Clearlake Capital, which holds a majority stake in Chelsea FC.
financials: ~$3.9B sale (Apr 2026) — an MLB record, ~8x revenue.
summary: The San Diego Padres are a Major League Baseball team based in San Diego, competing in the National League West and earning through tickets, media rights and sponsorships.

desc_simple: Sportsbox AI turns a normal smartphone camera into a 3D motion-capture coach — using AI to analyze a golfer's swing in three dimensions and give personalized feedback, drills and equipment tips through an app, without expensive lab equipment.
founders: Jeehae Lee, a former LPGA Tour player, and Samuel Menaker, a software engineer with 20+ years in AI.
financials: Eight-figure acquisition (Apr 2026); amount undisclosed.
summary: Sportsbox AI turns a normal smartphone camera into a 3D motion-capture coach — using AI to analyze a golfer's swing in three dimensions and give personalized feedback, drills and equipment tips through an app, without expensive lab equipment.

desc_simple: Urban Zoo builds technology tools and platforms used across the sports industry, supporting the behind-the-scenes technical setup sports organizations rely on to run.
financials: £20M growth investment from BGF (Jul 2026).
summary: Urban Zoo builds technology tools and platforms used across the sports industry, supporting the behind-the-scenes technical setup sports organizations rely on to run.

desc_simple: ENGO makes smart eyewear for athletes — glasses that display useful information like performance data right in front of the wearer's eyes while training or competing.
financials: €5.1M raise (Jul 2026).
summary: ENGO makes smart eyewear for athletes — glasses that display useful information like performance data right in front of the wearer's eyes while training or competing.

desc_simple: Refr Sports makes software that helps sports leagues manage their referees — handling scheduling and assigning officials to games so the right referees show up at the right place and time.
financials: $1M raise (Jul 2026).
summary: Refr Sports makes software that helps sports leagues manage their referees — handling scheduling and assigning officials to games so the right referees show up at the right place and time.

desc_simple: XbotGo makes smart, AI-powered cameras for filming sports games — the cameras automatically follow the action on the field or court and record it without needing a person to operate them.
financials: ~$14M Series A (May 2026).
summary: XbotGo makes smart, AI-powered cameras for filming sports games — the cameras automatically follow the action on the field or court and record it without needing a person to operate them.

desc_simple: SpeedLabs builds a real-time market engine for sports, powering fast-moving in-play markets (including a product called Momentum Markets) that shift as games are actually being played.
financials: $6.5M seed (Jun 2026).
summary: SpeedLabs builds a real-time market engine for sports, powering fast-moving in-play markets (including a product called Momentum Markets) that shift as games are actually being played.

desc_simple: Hexis runs a personalized nutrition platform for elite athletes, giving them customized eating and fueling plans built around their training and performance needs.
financials: $2.1M seed (Jun 2026).
summary: Hexis runs a personalized nutrition platform for elite athletes, giving them customized eating and fueling plans built around their training and performance needs.

desc_simple: VisioLab provides self-service checkout technology for stadiums and venues, letting people quickly pay for food and goods on their own to move lines faster at busy events.
financials: $11M Series A (Apr 2026).
summary: VisioLab provides self-service checkout technology for stadiums and venues, letting people quickly pay for food and goods on their own to move lines faster at busy events.

desc_simple: ProphetX runs a website where people trade on what they think will happen in sports. Instead of betting against a bookmaker, users buy and sell contracts with each other, and the price moves based on how likely an outcome looks. It's cleared to operate across the US under federal rules.
founders: Dean Sisun, co-founder and CEO.
financials: $35M growth round (Jul 2026).
summary: ProphetX runs a website where people trade on what they think will happen in sports. Instead of betting against a bookmaker, users buy and sell contracts with each other, and the price moves based on how likely an outcome looks. It's cleared to operate across the US under federal rules.

desc_simple: Underdog is an app where sports fans play daily fantasy games and trade on predictions about how games and players will do. Users pick outcomes and can win money if their guesses are right — one of the biggest sports prediction platforms in the US.
founders: Jeremy Levine, co-founder and CEO, who earlier started fantasy companies DRAFT and StarStreet.
financials: Acquired by IG Group for up to $1.3B (Jul 2026); ~$466M net revenue in the year to Jun 2026.
summary: Underdog is an app where sports fans play daily fantasy games and trade on predictions about how games and players will do. Users pick outcomes and can win money if their guesses are right — one of the biggest sports prediction platforms in the US.

desc_simple: LIV Golf is a professional golf league where top golfers compete in tournaments worldwide, mixing team and individual play in a shorter, faster format aimed at younger fans. Under a new plan, the golfers themselves would own most of the league.
financials: New investment/ownership restructuring reported Aug 2026; terms undisclosed.
summary: LIV Golf is a professional golf league where top golfers compete in tournaments worldwide, mixing team and individual play in a shorter, faster format aimed at younger fans. Under a new plan, the golfers themselves would own most of the league.

desc_simple: Legacy Motor Club is a NASCAR team that races stock cars in America's top motorsport series, fielding cars and drivers that compete against other teams on tracks across the country.
financials: New investor group (led by Sam Byrne, with athlete investors) took a stake (Jul 2026).
summary: Legacy Motor Club is a NASCAR team that races stock cars in America's top motorsport series, fielding cars and drivers that compete against other teams on tracks across the country.

desc_simple: The Wilmington Blue Rocks are a minor-league baseball team in Delaware — a development affiliate where younger players compete and improve on their way toward the major leagues.
financials: Acquired by OnDeck Partners with Avenue Sports Fund (Jul 2026); terms undisclosed.
summary: The Wilmington Blue Rocks are a minor-league baseball team in Delaware — a development affiliate where younger players compete and improve on their way toward the major leagues.

desc_simple: Free Agent is an online platform that helps athletes connect with each other and with people in business — a place to network, find opportunities and build careers off the field.
financials: $1.7M seed (Jul 2026).
summary: Free Agent is an online platform that helps athletes connect with each other and with people in business — a place to network, find opportunities and build careers off the field.
